15	export const meta = {
16	  name: 'datum-tdd-act',
17	  description: 'Deterministic TDD Act: RED->GREEN->REFACTOR per lane with gate enforcement',
18	  phases: [
19	    { title: 'Topology', detail: 'parse lane-plan.json, BFS wave grouping, auto-partition into ≤5 task batches' },
20	    { title: 'Setup', detail: 'create root + per-lane git worktrees (per batch)' },
21	    { title: 'Act', detail: 'RED->verify->GREEN->verify->REFACTOR per lane, wave-parallel (per batch)' },
22	    { title: 'Merge', detail: 'squash-merge lanes in topological order (per batch)' },
23	    { title: 'Cleanup', detail: 'remove worktrees (per batch)' },
24	    { title: 'Docs', detail: 'haiku pre-check + conditional sonnet sync (once after all batches)' },
25	    { title: 'Triage', detail: 'analyze failures, auto-file issues on the board' },

29	// ── Schemas ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
30

32	  type: 'object',

35	    commit_sha: { type: 'string' },
36	    files_written: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },

44	  properties: {

46	    reasoning: { type: 'string' },
47	    gaps: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
48	  },
49	  required: ['score', 'reasoning'],

51	
52	const SKEPTIC_SCHEMA = {
53	  type: 'object',
54	  properties: {
55	    bugs_found: { type: 'array', items: {
56	      type: 'object',
57	      properties: {

64	    confidence: { type: 'number' },
65	    verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['PASS', 'FRAGILE', 'BROKEN'] },
66	  },
67	  required: ['verdict'],

73	    issues: { type: 'array', items: {
74	      type: 'object',

98	// ── Wave builder (Kahn's algorithm) ──────────────────────────────────────────
99	
100	function buildWaves(lanePlan) {
101	  const lanes = lanePlan.lanes
102	  const ids = Object.keys(lanes)
103	  const inDeg = {}
104	  const adj = {}
105	
106	  for (const id of ids) {
107	    const deps = lanes[id].depends_on || []
108	    inDeg[id] = deps.length
109	    for (const dep of deps) {
110	      ;(adj[dep] = adj[dep] || []).push(id)
111	    }
112	  }
113	
114	  const waves = []
115	  let queue = ids.filter(id => inDeg[id] === 0).sort()
116	
117	  while (queue.length > 0) {
118	    waves.push([...queue])
119	    const next = []
120	    for (const id of queue) {
121	      for (const child of adj[id] || []) {
122	        inDeg[child]--
123	        if (inDeg[child] === 0) next.push(child)
124	      }
125	    }
126	    queue = next.sort()
127	  }
128	
129	  return waves
130	}

132	// ── File classification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
133	
134	function classifyFiles(files) {
135	  const isTest = f => {
136	    const base = f.split('/').pop()
137	    return base.startsWith('test_') || base.endsWith('_test.py') ||
138	      base.endsWith('.test.ts') || base.endsWith('.test.js') ||
139	      base.endsWith('.spec.ts') || base.endsWith('.spec.js') ||
140	      base.endsWith('_test.go') || base.endsWith('Tests.swift') ||
141	      f.includes('/tests/') || f.includes('/Tests/') ||
142	      base === 'conftest.py'
143	  }
144	  const testFiles = (files || []).filter(isTest)
145	  const implFiles = (files || []).filter(f => !isTest(f))
146	  return { testFiles, implFiles }
147	}
148	
149	// ── Text-to-JSON parser for datum-cli agents ───────────────────────────────
150	
151	function parseAgentJson(text, fallback) {
152	  if (!text || typeof text !== 'string') return fallback || null
153	  const cleaned = text.replace(/```[a-z]*\n?/g, '').trim()
154	  const start = cleaned.search(/[{[]/)
155	  const end = Math.max(cleaned.lastIndexOf('}'), cleaned.lastIndexOf(']'))
156	  if (start === -1 || end === -1) return fallback || null
157	  try { return JSON.parse(cleaned.slice(start, end + 1)) }
158	  catch { return fallback || null }
159	}

161	// ── Lane context shell command builder ─────────────────────────────────────
162	
163	function laneCtxCmd(packet, wt) {
164	  const ctx = JSON.stringify({
165	    task_id: packet.task_id,
166	    stage: packet.stage,
167	    allowed_write_files: packet.allowed_write_files,
168	    forbidden_write_files: packet.forbidden_write_files,
169	    commit_prefix: packet.commit_prefix,
170	    test_count_floor: 0,
171	  })
172	  return `mkdir -p "${wt}/.datum" && printf '%s' '${ctx.replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}' > "${wt}/.datum/lane-context.json"`
173	}
174	
175	// ── JSON packet builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
176	
177	function buildPacket(taskId, testFiles, implFiles, lane, wt, cfg, stage, extras) {
178	  return {
179	    schema_version: '1.0',
180	    task_id: taskId,
181	    stage,
182	    title: lane.title,
183	    working_directory: wt,
184	    test_command: cfg.testCommand,
185	    acceptance_criteria: lane.acceptance_criteria || [],
186	    red_note: lane.red_note || '',
187	    allowed_write_files: stage === 'RED' ? testFiles
188	      : stage === 'GREEN' ? implFiles
189	      : [...testFiles, ...implFiles],
190	    forbidden_write_files: stage === 'RED' ? implFiles
191	      : stage === 'GREEN' ? testFiles
192	      : [],
193	    commit_prefix: stage === 'RED' ? `red(${taskId})`
194	      : stage === 'GREEN' ? `green(${taskId})`
195	      : `refactor(${taskId})`,
196	    ...extras,
197	  }
198	}
199	
200	// ── Per-lane TDD saga ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	
202	async function runLane(taskId, lanePlan, worktreePaths, cfg) {
203	  const lane = lanePlan.lanes[taskId]
204	  const wt = worktreePaths[taskId]
205	  const isStructural = lane.stage === 'structural'
206	
207	  // #5: compute once per lane
208	  const { testFiles, implFiles } = classifyFiles(lane.files)
209	  const acStr = (lane.acceptance_criteria || []).join('\n')
210	
211	  // Per-lane test command: only run THIS lane's test files, not the global set
212	  const laneTestCmd = testFiles.length > 0
213	    ? `uv run pytest ${testFiles.join(' ')} -x -q`
214	    : cfg.testCommand
215	  const laneCfg = { ...cfg, testCommand: laneTestCmd }
216	
217	  log(`[${taskId}] Starting: ${lane.title} (${isStructural ? 'structural' : 'behavioral'})`)
218	
219	  if (isStructural) {
220	    const r = await runRefactor(taskId, lane, testFiles, implFiles, wt, laneCfg)
221	    if (!r) return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'REFACTOR', error: 'refactor failed' }
222	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'completed' }
223	  }
224	
225	  // ── Skeleton preflight (E2: capture output directly, no separate read agent) ──
226	  const skeletonText = await agent(
227	    `cd "${wt}" && datum skeleton --task-id ${taskId} --language ${cfg.language} ` +
228	    `--tasks ${cfg.lanePlanPath} --output .datum/runs/${cfg.runId}/preflight-${taskId}.json 2>&1`,
229	    { label: `skeleton:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku', agentType: 'datum-cli' }
230	  )
231	  const preflight = parseAgentJson(skeletonText, {})
232	
233	  // ── RED ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
234	  log(`[${taskId}] RED: writing failing tests`)
235	
236	  const redPacket = buildPacket(taskId, testFiles, implFiles, lane, wt, laneCfg, 'RED', {})
237	  const redPacketStr = JSON.stringify(redPacket)
238	  const redCtxCmd = laneCtxCmd(redPacket, wt)
239	
240	  let red = await agent(
241	    `You are a RED TDD agent. Write FAILING tests for the acceptance criteria.\n` +
242	    `SETUP (run first): ${redCtxCmd}\n` +
243	    `TASK PACKET: ${redPacketStr}\n\n` +
244	    `CRITICAL RULES:\n` +
245	    `- cd into working_directory before any operation\n` +
246	    `- APPEND new test functions — NEVER delete existing tests\n` +
247	    `- NEVER use raise NotImplementedError — conftest will xfail it and tests pass (green blindness)\n` +
248	    `- Instead, CALL the actual methods that don't exist yet (e.g., result.to_dict()) — AttributeError is the correct RED failure\n` +
249	    `- Run test_command — your new tests MUST FAIL with AttributeError or AssertionError\n` +
250	    `- Commit with message: "${redPacket.commit_prefix}: <description>"`,
251	    { label: `red:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'sonnet', schema: STAGE_RESULT_SCHEMA }
252	  )
253	
254	  if (!red || !red.committed) {
255	    log(`[${taskId}] RED attempt 1 failed, retrying with hint`)
256	    red = await agent(
257	      `SETUP (run first): ${redCtxCmd}\n` +
258	      `TASK PACKET: ${redPacketStr}\n\n` +
259	      `RETRY HINT: Previous attempt failed (${(red && red.failure_reason) || 'no commit'}). ` +
260	      `Focus on writing simple, concrete assertions that test the acceptance criteria directly. ` +
261	      `Do not overthink — one test per AC, assert specific values.`,
262	      { label: `red-retry:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'sonnet', schema: STAGE_RESULT_SCHEMA }
263	    )
264	  }
265	
266	  if (!red || !red.committed) {
267	    const err = (red && red.failure_reason) || 'RED agent did not commit after 2 attempts'
268	    log(`[${taskId}] RED FAILED: ${err}`)
269	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'RED', error: err }
270	  }
271	
272	  // ── Verify RED ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
273	  const redCheckText = await agent(
274	    `cd "${wt}" && datum verify-stage red --repo "${wt}" --test-command "${laneCfg.testCommand}"\nReturn ONLY the JSON output, nothing else.`,
275	    { label: `verify-red:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku', agentType: 'datum-cli' }
276	  )
277	  const redCheck = parseAgentJson(redCheckText, { verified: false })
278	
279	  if (!redCheck || !redCheck.verified) {
280	    const err = (redCheck && redCheck.error) || 'green_blindness_violation: tests passed after RED'
281	    log(`[${taskId}] RED FAILED: ${err}`)
282	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'RED', error: err }
283	  }
284	  log(`[${taskId}] RED verified`)
285	
286	  // ── Reflect on test quality ───────────────────────────────────────────
287	  const reflect = await agent(
288	    `Read these test files in "${wt}": ${testFiles.join(', ')}\n` +
289	    `Score the tests written for these acceptance criteria:\n${acStr}\n` +
290	    `Return your score (0-10), reasoning, and gaps found.`,
291	    { label: `reflect:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku', schema: REFLECT_SCHEMA }
292	  )
293	
294	  const reflectScore = (reflect && reflect.score) || 0
295	  log(`[${taskId}] Test quality score: ${reflectScore}/10`)
296	  if (reflectScore < 4) {
297	    log(`[${taskId}] RED FAILED: test quality too low (${reflectScore}/10): ${reflect && reflect.reasoning}`)
298	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'RED', error: `test quality ${reflectScore}/10` }
299	  }
300	
301	  // ── Context for GREEN (E2+E8+E10+E11: signal from verify-red, preflight from skeleton, no extra agents) ──
302	  const signal = (redCheck && redCheck.test_signal) || { exit_code: 1, errors: [], assertion_messages: [] }
303	
304	  // E8: extract contract_summary from ACs deterministically
305	  const BUILTIN_SKIP = new Set(['print','len','str','int','dict','list','set','isinstance','type','exit','round','sorted','filter','map','any','all','range','enumerate','zip','open','input','format','repr','hash','id','dir','vars','super','property','staticmethod','classmethod'])
306	  const contractSummary = (lane.acceptance_criteria || []).map(ac => {
307	    const funcMatch = ac.match(/(?<!['"-])(\w+)\(([^)]*)\)/)
308	    const retMatch = ac.match(/returns?\s+(?:a\s+)?(\w+)/i)
309	    const raiseMatch = ac.match(/[Rr]aises?\s+(\w+Error|\w+Exception)/)
310	    if (!funcMatch || BUILTIN_SKIP.has(funcMatch[1])) return null
311	    return {
312	      function: funcMatch[1],
313	      args: funcMatch[2] ? funcMatch[2].split(',').map(a => a.trim()).filter(Boolean) : [],
314	      returns: retMatch ? retMatch[1] : null,
315	      raises: raiseMatch ? raiseMatch[1] : null,
316	      ac: ac.slice(0, 120),
317	    }
318	  }).filter(Boolean)
319	
320	  // ── GREEN (sonnet first, opus on retry) ───────────────────────────────
321	  log(`[${taskId}] GREEN: making tests pass`)
322	
323	  const greenModel = lane.green_model || 'sonnet'
324	
325	  const greenPacket = buildPacket(taskId, testFiles, implFiles, lane, wt, laneCfg, 'GREEN', {
326	    test_signal: signal,
327	    preflight: preflight,
328	    contract_summary: contractSummary,
329	    impl_stubs: preflight.impl_stubs || [],
330	    existing_api: preflight.existing_api || {},
331	  })
332	  const greenPacketStr = JSON.stringify(greenPacket)
333	  const greenCtxCmd = laneCtxCmd(greenPacket, wt)
334	
335	  let green = await agent(
336	    `SETUP (run first): ${greenCtxCmd}\n` +
337	    `TASK PACKET: ${greenPacketStr}\n\n` +
338	    `CONTEXT:\n` +
339	    `- contract_summary: structured function signatures extracted from ACs — implement these\n` +
340	    `- impl_stubs: stub files already created with function signatures and ... bodies — fill them in\n` +
341	    `- existing_api: skeleton of existing module code — understand the API shape before extending\n` +
342	    `- red_note: what behaviors the tests check for\n` +
343	    `- test_signal: error messages from failing tests\n` +
344	    `Write MINIMUM code to make tests pass — nothing more.`,
345	    { label: `green:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: greenModel, schema: STAGE_RESULT_SCHEMA }
346	  )
347	
348	  if (!green || !green.committed) {
349	    const escalatedModel = 'opus'
350	    log(`[${taskId}] GREEN attempt 1 failed (${greenModel}), retrying with ${escalatedModel}`)
351	
352	    // Reset worktree to clean RED state — partial impl from failed attempt contaminates signal
353	    await agent(
354	      `cd "${wt}" && git checkout -- . && git clean -fd --exclude=.datum/`,
355	      { label: `reset-green:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku', agentType: 'datum-cli' }
356	    )
357	
358	    const retryCheckText = await agent(
359	      `cd "${wt}" && datum verify-stage red --repo "${wt}" --test-command "${laneCfg.testCommand}"\nReturn ONLY the JSON output, nothing else.`,
360	      { label: `signal-retry:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku', agentType: 'datum-cli' }
361	    )
362	    const retryCheck = parseAgentJson(retryCheckText, {})
363	    const retrySignal = (retryCheck && retryCheck.test_signal) || signal
364	    const retryPacket = buildPacket(taskId, testFiles, implFiles, lane, wt, laneCfg, 'GREEN', {
365	      test_signal: retrySignal,
366	      preflight: preflight,
367	      contract_summary: contractSummary,
368	      impl_stubs: preflight.impl_stubs || [],
369	      existing_api: preflight.existing_api || {},
370	      retry_hint: `Previous attempt failed: ${(green && green.failure_reason) || 'no commit'}. Read the FULL error output carefully. Fix the implementation.`,
371	    })
372	    green = await agent(
373	      `SETUP (run first): ${greenCtxCmd}\n` +
374	      `TASK PACKET: ${JSON.stringify(retryPacket)}\n\n` +
375	      `CONTEXT: RETRY — previous attempt failed. Read existing implementation files.\n` +
376	      `- contract_summary: function signatures to implement\n` +
377	      `- impl_stubs/existing_api: fill in bodies, don't start from scratch\n` +

380	    )
381	  }
382	
383	  if (!green || !green.committed) {
384	    const err = (green && green.failure_reason) || 'GREEN agent did not commit after 2 attempts'
385	    log(`[${taskId}] GREEN FAILED: ${err}`)
386	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'GREEN', error: err }
387	  }
388	
389	  // ── Verify GREEN ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

391	    `cd "${wt}" && datum verify-stage green --repo "${wt}" --test-command "${laneCfg.testCommand}"\nReturn ONLY the JSON output, nothing else.`,
392	    { label: `verify-green:${taskId}`, phase: 'Act', model: 'haiku', agentType: 'datum-cli' }
393	  )

395	
396	  if (!greenCheck || !greenCheck.verified) {
397	    const err = (greenCheck && greenCheck.error) || 'tests still failing after GREEN'

400	  }
401	  log(`[${taskId}] GREEN verified`)
402	
403	  // ── Adversarial skeptic panel (3 lenses, parallel, consensus) ───────
404	  const skepticBase =
405	    `Working directory: "${wt}"\n` +
406	    `Implementation files: ${implFiles.join(', ')}\n` +
407	    `Test files: ${testFiles.join(', ')}\n` +
408	    `Test command: ${cfg.testCommand}\n` +
409	    `Acceptance criteria:\n${acStr}\n\n`
410	
411	  const SKEPTIC_LENSES = [

413	    { key: 'error', model: 'haiku', prompt: 'LENS: Error paths. Focus on exception handling, invalid state transitions, missing validation, what happens when preconditions are violated.' },
414	    { key: 'contract', model: 'sonnet', prompt: 'LENS: Behavioral contracts. Does the implementation ACTUALLY satisfy the acceptance criteria, or does it just make the specific tests pass? Look for cases where the ACs are met literally but not in spirit.' },
415	  ]
416	
417	  const skepticResults = await parallel(
418	    SKEPTIC_LENSES.map(lens => () =>
419	      agent(

422	      )
423	    )

426	  const allBugs = []

435	  }

437	  const bugDescs = allBugs.map(b => b.description.toLowerCase().slice(0, 60))

443	  if (brokenCount >= 2) {

445	    log(`[${taskId}] SKEPTIC PANEL: ${brokenCount}/3 BROKEN — ${crossValidated.length} cross-validated bugs: ${bugList || 'none'}`)
446	  } else if (brokenCount === 1) {
447	    log(`[${taskId}] SKEPTIC PANEL: 1/3 BROKEN (no consensus) — proceeding`)
448	  } else {

450	  }
451	
452	  // ── File ownership check ──────────────────────────────────────────────
453	  const allAllowed = new Set([...testFiles, ...implFiles])
454	  const writtenFiles = [...(red.files_written || []), ...(green.files_written || [])]
455	  const violations = writtenFiles.filter(f => !allAllowed.has(f))
456	  if (violations.length > 0) {
457	    log(`[${taskId}] FILE OWNERSHIP VIOLATION: ${violations.join(', ')}`)
458	  }

461	  const refResult = await runRefactor(taskId, lane, testFiles, implFiles, wt, laneCfg)
462	  if (!refResult) {
463	    return { task_id: taskId, status: 'failed', stage: 'REFACTOR', error: 'refactor failed' }
464	  }

466	  log(`[${taskId}] Lane complete`)
467	  return { task_id: taskId, status: 'completed' }

470	// #4: conditional refactor — haiku pre-check before sonnet call
471	async function runRefactor(taskId, lane, testFiles, implFiles, wt, cfg) {
472	  log(`[${taskId}] REFACTOR: checking if needed`)

@app.command(name="tdd-args")
def tdd_args_cmd(
    feature: str = typer.Option(
        "",
        "--feature",
        help="Feature name to use as the epic branch base. Defaults to current git branch.",
    ),
    lane_plan: str = typer.Option(
        ".datum/lane-plan.json",
        "--lane-plan",
        help="Path to lane-plan.json",
    ),
    repo: str = typer.Option(".", "--repo", help="Repository root (default: cwd)"),
):
    """Emit structured TDD workflow arguments as JSON.

    Outputs a JSON object with epicBranch, runId, lanePlanPath, testCommand,
    and language — ready for consumption by the TDD driver loop.

    Examples:

      datum tdd-args --feature "BETA / GA"

      datum tdd-args

    """
    import re
    import subprocess
    from datetime import datetime

    # Resolve feature name: --feature is required.
    if not feature:
        typer.echo(
            "Error: --feature is required. Provide the feature name, e.g.:\n"
            '  datum tdd-args --feature "My Feature"',
            err=False,
        )
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    # Sanitize feature name into a git branch slug.
    slug = feature.lower()
    slug = slug.replace(" ", "-")
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9\-_]", "", slug)
    slug = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", slug)
    slug = slug.strip("-")
    slug = slug[:64]

    epic_branch = f"feat/{slug}"

    run_id = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")

    # Detect test command.
    repo_root = Path(repo).resolve()
    pyproject_path = repo_root / "pyproject.toml"
    test_command = "uv run pytest -x -q"
    if pyproject_path.exists():
        try:
            content = pyproject_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

---
name: datum-tdd
description: "Launch the datum TDD pipeline on a feature. Takes a feature description or GitHub issue, decomposes it into tasks with acceptance criteria, generates lane-plan.json, creates the epic branch, and fires the workflow. Use this skill whenever the user wants to implement a feature using TDD, says 'datum tdd', 'run tdd on', 'implement this with tests', or references a GitHub issue they want to build with the datum pipeline."
---

# datum-tdd: Feature → TDD Pipeline

This skill bridges the gap between "I want to build X" and the deterministic
`datum-tdd-act` workflow. It handles everything the workflow needs as input.

## When to use

- User says "datum tdd", "tdd this", "implement with tdd"
- User references a GitHub issue and wants it built
- User describes a feature and wants tests-first implementation
- User says "run the pipeline on this"

## Input

One of:
- A feature description in natural language
- A GitHub issue number (e.g., `#42`)
- A file path to a spec or task list

## What this skill produces

1. **Lane plan** (`.datum/lane-plan.json`) — tasks, ACs, file ownership, dependencies
2. **Epic branch** (`git branch <name> HEAD`)
3. **Workflow launch** — fires `datum-tdd-act` with the correct args

## Step 1: Gather the feature spec

If the user gave an issue number, fetch it:
```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue view <number> --json title,body,labels
```

If the user gave a description, use it directly. If it's vague, ask ONE
clarifying question — don't interview. Bias toward action.

## Step 2: Decompose into tasks

Break the feature into 2-5 tasks. Each task needs:

- **id**: `task-001`, `task-002`, etc.
- **title**: what this task implements (one sentence)
- **files**: which source and test files this task touches
- **acceptance_criteria**: 2-4 specific, testable ACs starting with "AC1:", "AC2:", etc.
- **red_note**: hint for the RED agent on what tests to write
- **stage**: `behavioral` (needs RED→GREEN) or `structural` (refactor only)
- **depends_on**: list of task IDs this depends on (for wave ordering)
- **estimated_impl_lines**: estimated lines of implementation code GREEN will write (split task if >30)
- **green_model**: optional model override for GREEN agent (e.g., "opus" for complex tasks)

Guidelines for good decomposition:
- Each task should be independently testable
- File ownership should be clear — avoid two tasks writing to the same file in the same wave
- Dependencies create waves — independent tasks run in parallel, dependent tasks sequence
- ACs must be specific enough that a test can verify them (values, not vibes)
- red_note should tell RED what methods/classes to call that don't exist yet

## Step 3: Detect target files

Use the codebase to figure out which files each task touches:
- Grep for the module/class being extended
- Check if test files already exist or need creation
- Verify paths are correct (don't invent files)

## Step 4: Generate lane-plan.json

Write `.datum/lane-plan.json` with this structure:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "total_lanes": <number of tasks>,
  "topological_order": ["task-001", "task-002", ...],
  "file_ownership": {
    "src/module.py": "task-001",
    "tests/test_module.py": "task-001"
  },
  "lanes": {
    "task-001": {
      "id": "task-001",
      "title": "...",
      "files": ["src/module.py", "tests/test_module.py"],
      "acceptance_criteria": ["AC1: ...", "AC2: ..."],
      "red_note": "...",
      "stage": "behavioral",
      "depends_on": [],
      "estimated_impl_lines": 20,
      "green_model": null
    }
  }
}
```

The `topological_order` must respect `depends_on` — a task's dependencies must
appear before it in the list.

## Step 5: Create epic branch and run ID

```bash
git branch <epic-branch-name> HEAD
```

Branch naming: `feat/<short-kebab-description>` or `fix/<short-kebab-description>`.
Run ID: date-based, e.g., `20260613-feat-serialization`.

## Step 6: Detect test command

Look at the project to determine the right test command:
- Python with pytest: `uv run pytest tests/<test_file>.py -x -q`
- Python with unittest: `uv run python -m unittest tests/<test_file>.py`
- Check `pyproject.toml` for test configuration

## Step 7: Launch the workflow

```
Workflow({
  scriptPath: "<repo>/skills/datum-tdd-act.js",
  args: {
    lanePlanPath: ".datum/lane-plan.json",
    epicBranch: "<branch-name>",
    runId: "<run-id>",
    testCommand: "<detected test command>",
    language: "<python|typescript|swift|etc>"
  }
})
```

## Step 8: Report

Tell the user:
- What tasks were created and their wave grouping
- The epic branch name
- That the workflow is running (use `/workflows` to watch)

## Important constraints

- Plans with >5 tasks are auto-partitioned into sequential batches of ≤5 by the workflow — no manual splitting needed
- NEVER let estimated_impl_lines exceed 30 for any task — split the task if the implementation would be larger
- For large features (>10 tasks), group tasks into logical units with clear dependency boundaries between groups
- NEVER guess file paths — verify they exist with `ls` or `find`
- NEVER put two tasks in the same wave if they write to the same file
- NEVER assign an EXISTING test file (one with passing tests) to a task — always create a NEW test file per feature so verify-red can detect failures cleanly
- The test command must work FROM A WORKTREE (the workflow creates git worktrees)
- ACs must be testable by calling actual code — no "should be well-structured" vibes
- red_note MUST say "Create a NEW file" for the test file and "NEVER use raise NotImplementedError"

file.content:
"""workflow-dashboard.py — Real-time web dashboard for datum TDD workflows.

Serves a single-page dashboard on port 10001 that shows inflight workflow
progress by scanning Claude Code's workflow transcript directories.

Usage:
    python scripts/workflow-dashboard.py [--port 10001]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from http.server import HTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

CLAUDE_PROJECTS = Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects"
PORT = int(os.environ.get("DASHBOARD_PORT", "10001"))


def find_workflow_dirs() -> list[dict]:
    """Scan all Claude project dirs for workflow transcript directories."""
    runs = []
    if not CLAUDE_PROJECTS.exists():
        return runs
    for project in CLAUDE_PROJECTS.iterdir():
        if not project.is_dir():
            continue
        for session in project.iterdir():
            wf_base = session / "subagents" / "workflows"
            if not wf_base.exists():
                continue
            for wf_dir in sorted(wf_base.iterdir(), reverse=True):
                if wf_dir.is_dir() and wf_dir.name.startswith("wf_"):
                    runs.append(
                        {
                            "id": wf_dir.name,
                            "path": str(wf_dir),
                            "project": project.name[:40],
                            "mtime": wf_dir.stat().st_mtime,
                        }
                    )
    runs.sort(key=lambda r: r["mtime"], reverse=True)
    return runs[:20]


def scan_workflow(wf_path: str) -> dict:
    """Read agent meta files and transcript sizes for a workflow."""
    wf = Path(wf_path)
    agents = []
    for meta_file in sorted(wf.glob("agent-*.meta.json")):
        agent_id = meta_file.stem.replace(".meta", "")
        transcript = wf / f"{agent_id}.jsonl"
        meta = {}
        try:
            meta = json.loads(meta_file.read_text())
        except Exception:
            pass

        prompt_preview = ""
        try:
            with open(transcript) as f:
                first = json.loads(f.readline())
                content = first.get("message", {}).get("content", "")
                if isinstance(content, str):
                    prompt_preview = content[:120]
        except Exception:
            pass

        t_size = transcript.stat().st_size if transcript.exists() else 0
        t_mtime = transcript.stat().st_mtime if transcript.exists() else 0
        is_active = (time.time() - t_mtime) < 30 if t_mtime else False

        agents.append(
            {
                "id": agent_id,
                "type": meta.get("agentType", "unknown"),
                "size_kb": round(t_size / 1024, 1),
                "active": is_active,
                "prompt": prompt_preview,
                "mtime": t_mtime,
            }
        )

    agents.sort(key=lambda a: a["mtime"])
    total_kb = sum(a["size_kb"] for a in agents)
    active_count = sum(1 for a in agents if a["active"])

    return {
        "id": wf.name,
        "agents": agents,
        "total_agents": len(agents),
        "active_agents": active_count,
        "total_kb": round(total_kb, 1),
    }

- **reset** — Universal box-sizing reset, body baseline

- **components** — All styled elements (cards, buttons, tables, badges, forms)

- `@media (max-width: 900px)` — responsive grid collapse
- `@keyframes` — `pulse` and `spin` animations
- `color-mix(in srgb, ...)` — modern color mixing (non-Tailwind feature)
- `grid-template-rows: 0fr` → `1fr` transition — smooth expand/collapse
- `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` — table number alignment

**Size:** 159 lines of CSS, well-commented, production-ready

### 3. JavaScript Visualization: Bell Curve Distribution

**Canvas Drawing:** Lines 615–686 (`drawBell` function)

**What it does:**
- Renders a **histogram + KDE density curve** for token/duration distributions
- Plots bars for 30 bins across the dataset
- Overlays a **smooth kernel density estimation curve** (Gaussian)
- Adds reference lines: **median (green dashed)** and **mean (yellow dotted)**
- Includes axes labels with formatted numbers
- Fully custom canvas context drawing — no chart library

**Key features:**
- High-DPI canvas support (`devicePixelRatio`)
- Manual KDE calculation (bandwidth = range/10, Gaussian kernel)
- Canvas transformation for responsive sizing

This is **NOT** a simple visualization — it's sophisticated statistical plotting that would benefit from a dedicated library.

### 4. Data Flow & API

**Three REST endpoints:**
1. `GET /api/runs` — Returns list of 30 most recent workflow runs
2. `GET /api/detail?path=...` — Loads full workflow state for detail view
3. `GET /api/metrics` — Aggregates stats across all runs
   - Returns: models, phases, token_distribution (array), duration_distribution (array)
   - Includes computed metrics: medians, percentiles, retry rates, success rates

Data fetched every **2 seconds** (sidebar refresh) and on-demand (detail/metrics tabs).

### 5. Frontend Tooling Status

**Current State:**
- No `package.json` in project root
- No Tailwind config anywhere in main repo
- No npm/Node.js build pipeline for the dashboard
- No TypeScript
- **Zero build dependencies**

The dashboard is a **pure vanilla HTML/CSS/JS file** served by Python.

### 6. Tailwind CSS Integration Options

For a **single inline HTML page in a Python server**, here's the viability matrix:

| Option | Build Step | CDN | File Size | Best For |
|--------|-----------|-----|-----------|----------|
| **Tailwind CDN (Play)** | ✗ Zero | ✓ Yes | ~10KB | Prototyping, demos, inline HTML |
| **Tailwind CLI (Standalone)** | ✓ Manual run | ✗ File-based | ~5KB output | Production single-file, no Node |
| **npm + Vite/Webpack** | ✓ Full build | ✗ No | ~3KB output | Multi-page apps, component frameworks |

**Recommendation:** **Tailwind CLI Standalone Binary**
- No Node.js required (single `tailwindcss` binary)
- One-time setup: `curl https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/releases/download/v3.x.x/tailwindcss-macos-arm64 -o tailwindcss && chmod +x tailwindcss`
- Usage: `./tailwindcss -i input.css -o dashboard.css --watch` (development)
- Gives you Tailwind's tree-shaking, optimized CSS output, production minification
- Can be integrated into `scripts/` workflow or CI

**Alternative (zero setup):** Tailwind Play CDN
- Add `<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>`
- No build step, but CSS is not optimized for production
- ~65KB download (full framework)
- Fine for development/testing; use CLI for prod

### 7. Stats Libraries: Zero-Build CDN Integration

For the **bell curve + metrics visualization**, here's what's viable via CDN:

| Library | Format | Size | Histograms | Distributions | CDN Ready | Notes |
|---------|--------|------|-----------|---------------|-----------|-------|
| **Chart.js** | UMD/ESM | 85KB | ✓ Bar | ✗ Limited | ✓ Yes | Good for simple distributions, popular |
| **Plotly.js** | UMD | 3.2MB | ✓ Bar + Histogram | ✓ Box/Violin | ✓ Yes (lite: 1.5MB) | Rich stats viz, full statistical plots |

  - Custom spacing → leverage Tailwind scales
  - Animation keyframes → `theme.extend.animation`
- Grid/flexbox already Tailwind-native
- Keep your CSS var philosophy but expose via Tailwind config

**Phase 3: Replace custom canvas with Chart.js**
- Replace `drawBell()` (72 lines) with Chart.js histogram
- Use Chart.js plugins for reference lines (median/mean)
- One `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js"></script>` tag
- ~5 lines of config JS replaces your KDE calculation

**Phase 4: Keep the Python backend unchanged**
- `/api/runs`, `/api/detail`, `/api/metrics` stay as-is
- Only the HTML/CSS/JS blob gets rewritten

---

| Metric | Current | Post-Migration (Tailwind + Chart.js) |
|--------|---------|------|
| Inline HTML size | 516 lines | ~450 lines (shorter CSS, simpler JS) |
| CSS lines | 159 | ~80–100 (Tailwind classes replace custom CSS) |

| CDN dependencies | 0 | 1–2 (Tailwind CLI output + Chart.js) |

| Production readiness | Full | Better (optimized CSS, battle-tested chart lib) |

---

### Viability Assessment

✓ **Fully viable** — The dashboard is a perfect candidate for this migration:
- Clean CSS architecture (already using `@layer`)
- Simple DOM structure (no complex frameworks)
- Contained visualization (one canvas element)
- No existing build tooling (clean slate)
- Single-file deployment (easy to manage)

The migration is **low-risk** and **backwards-compatible** — you can do it incrementally without breaking the Python server.

# Plan: Dashboard → Tailwind CSS + Chart.js

## Context

The workflow dashboard (`scripts/workflow-dashboard.py`) uses 159 lines of custom CSS with `@layer`, custom properties, and `color-mix()`. The bell curve visualization is 72 lines of manual canvas drawing. The user wants Tailwind for styling and a proper stats/charting library for the distribution graphs.

---

## Approach

**Tailwind**: CDN Play script (`<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com">`). Zero build step, works in inline HTML. Custom colors/fonts via inline `tailwind.config`.

**Chart.js + annotation plugin**: Two CDN scripts. Replaces the custom `drawBell()` canvas code with a histogram + KDE line chart + median/mean annotation lines. Adds tooltips and responsive resize for free.

---

## What Changes

### File: `scripts/workflow-dashboard.py`

**1. Add 3 CDN tags to `<head>`**
- Tailwind CDN play script + inline config (custom colors, fonts from existing CSS vars)
- Chart.js 4.x UMD
- chartjs-plugin-annotation 3.x

**2. Replace `<style>` block (159 → ~25 lines)**

Keep only what Tailwind can't express:
- `grid-template-rows: 0fr/1fr` expand/collapse animation
- `@keyframes pulse, spin`
- `.spinner` component (8px custom sizing)
- `[data-status="running"] .phase-dot` pulse

Delete everything else — Tailwind utilities replace it.

**3. Rewrite HTML structure with Tailwind classes**

All semantic class names → utility strings. Key mappings:
- `--bg-card: #12121a` → `bg-bg-card` (via theme config)
- `color-mix(in srgb, var(--green) 15%, transparent)` → `bg-green/15`
- Grid layouts → `grid grid-cols-[320px_1fr]`

# Plan: datum-tdd-act Workflow Script (issue #133)

## Context

The datum Act phase is currently manual: the LLM reads SKILL.md and reference docs, then dispatches RED/GREEN/REFACTOR agents by hand. This produced 8 friction issues in epic-30 (#125-#132): green blindness, scope violations, file conflicts, manual DAG tracking.

Issue #133 converts this into a **deterministic Workflow script** — a JS orchestrator that reads `lane-plan.json` and fans out tasks through the full TDD pipeline with enforced gates.

Prerequisites on main: `worktree_manager.py` (#137), `_execute_tool` worktree routing (#137), `tdd_driver.py` (RED/GREEN verification).

---

## Orchestration Architecture (Workflow Patterns Applied)

**Pattern: Fan-Out/Fan-In with Saga Compensation**

The TDD pipeline maps to these workflow orchestration patterns:

1. **Fan-Out/Fan-In** — tasks within a dependency wave run concurrently via `parallel()`, results aggregated at wave barrier before next wave dispatches. Per the scaling rule: keep each workflow bounded (one lane = one `runLane()` chain, not unbounded).

2. **Saga with Compensation** — each lane is a saga: RED → GREEN → REFACTOR. On failure at any stage, compensation fires (log failure, skip lane). No rollback needed because worktrees isolate changes — a failed lane's worktree is simply cleaned up without affecting the epic branch.

3. **Determinism** — the Workflow script is pure orchestration logic (decision-making, coordination). All external interactions (git, test runners, file I/O) happen through `agent()` calls (the "activities"). The script itself contains no I/O, no `Date.now()`, no randomness — compliant with workflow determinism constraints.

4. **Idempotency** — `verify-stage` is idempotent (run N times, same result). `setup_pipeline_worktrees` is NOT idempotent (second call fails on existing worktree) — acceptable since setup runs once per pipeline.

5. **Entity Lifecycle** — each lane worktree is an entity with a lifecycle: created (Setup) → used (Act) → merged (Merge) → destroyed (Cleanup). The `worktree_manager.py` module manages the full lifecycle.

---

## Design Decisions

### Wave-based parallel, not pipeline()

BFS-layer tasks via Kahn's algorithm. Within each wave: `parallel()` (barrier). Between waves: barrier ensures all prior RED+stub commits land before downstream waves start. `pipeline()` is unsuitable — no cross-item barrier, dependent tasks could start before deps finish.

### Pre-created persistent worktrees

`isolation: 'worktree'` creates FRESH worktrees per agent — tests from RED would vanish before GREEN. Instead: `setup_pipeline_worktrees()` creates one persistent worktree per lane. All three agents (RED/GREEN/REFACTOR) share the same worktree.

### Model tiers

| Agent | Model | Rationale |
|-------|-------|-----------|
| Topology, Setup, Skeleton, Verify, Merge, Cleanup | `haiku` | Mechanical, deterministic checks |
| RED, GREEN, REFACTOR | `sonnet` | Requires reasoning about code |

### v1 scope exclusions

Retry ladder, adversarial agent, security/docs sidecars, fine-grained GREEN-dep gating — all deferred to v2.

---

## What to Build

### 1. CLI commands in `datum/cli.py`

**Worktree sub-app** (calls existing `worktree_manager.py`):
```
datum worktrees setup   --run-id <id> --epic-branch <branch> --lane-ids <a,b,c>
datum worktrees merge   --epic-branch <branch> --lane-order <a,b,c> --commit-message <msg>
datum worktrees cleanup --run-id <id> --epic-branch <branch>
```

**Verify-stage** (calls existing `tdd_driver.py`):
```
datum verify-stage <red|green|baseline> [--repo .] [--test-command "pytest -q"]
```
- `red`: tests must FAIL (exit 0 if failing, exit 1 if passing = green blindness)
- `green`/`baseline`: tests must PASS (exit 0 if passing, exit 1 if failing)

### 2. Workflow script: `skills/datum-tdd-act.js`

```js
export const meta = {
  name: 'datum-tdd-act',
  description: 'Deterministic TDD Act: RED->GREEN->REFACTOR per lane with gate enforcement',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Topology', detail: 'parse lane-plan.json, BFS wave grouping' },
    { title: 'Setup', detail: 'create per-lane git worktrees' },
    { title: 'Act', detail: 'RED->verify->GREEN->verify->REFACTOR per lane, wave-parallel' },
    { title: 'Merge', detail: 'squash-merge lanes in topological order' },
    { title: 'Cleanup', detail: 'remove worktrees, prune stale refs' },
  ],
}
```

**Args**: `{ lanePlanPath, epicBranch, runId, testCommand, language }`

**`buildWaves(lanePlan)`** — Kahn's algorithm (BFS layers on `depends_on` edges).

**`runLane(taskId, ...)`** — the saga per lane:
```
structural → REFACTOR only
behavioral:
  1. Skeleton preflight (haiku)
  2. RED (sonnet) → verify-red (haiku, MUST fail) → fail-fast on green blindness
  3. Test signal extraction (haiku)
  4. GREEN (sonnet) → verify-green (haiku, MUST pass) → fail-fast if still failing
  5. REFACTOR (sonnet) → verify-refactor (haiku, MUST pass)
```

Failures: log to `.datum/runs/<RUN_ID>/act-failures.jsonl`, return null. Other lanes continue.

**Agent prompts** contain: role, worktree path, task entry, ACs, file permissions (RED: test files only, GREEN: impl files only, REFACTOR: all), properties, done condition with commit format.

### 3. `install.sh`

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude/workflows"
ln -sf "$DATUM_REPO/skills/datum-tdd-act.js" "$HOME/.claude/workflows/datum-tdd-act.js"
```

### 4. Tests

**`tests/test_tdd_cli_commands.py`** (12 tests):
- worktrees setup/merge/cleanup: 6 tests (happy path, error cases, idempotency)
- verify-stage: 6 tests (red-pass, red-fail/green-blindness, green-pass, green-fail, custom cmd, unknown stage)

**`tests/test_wave_builder.py`** (4 tests):
- independent tasks → single wave
- linear chain → N waves
- diamond DAG → 2 waves
- complex realistic DAG

---

## Files

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `datum/cli.py` | Add `worktrees` sub-app + `verify-stage` |
| `skills/datum-tdd-act.js` | New — Workflow script |
| `install.sh` | Add workflow symlink |
| `tests/test_tdd_cli_commands.py` | New — 12 tests |
| `tests/test_wave_builder.py` | New — 4 tests |

Reused (no changes): `datum/worktree_manager.py`, `datum/tdd_driver.py`

---

## Known gaps

1. Verify if `agent()` supports `cwd:` — if not, worktree path is prompt-only
2. `depends_on` lives in `tasks.json` not `lane-plan.json` — Topology agent reads both
3. Commit queue not needed for v1 (worktrees eliminate index contention)
4. Post-commit file-ownership check (prompt-only enforcement for v1)

## Verification

1. `uv run pytest tests/test_tdd_cli_commands.py tests/test_wave_builder.py -v` — 16 pass
2. `uv run pytest tests/test_tdd_driver.py -v` — existing pass
3. `bash install.sh` — workflow symlink created
4. `datum worktrees setup --help` / `datum verify-stage --help` — correct flags
5. `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — full suite green

"""workflow-dashboard.py — Real-time web dashboard for datum TDD workflows.

Serves a single-page dashboard on port 10001 that shows inflight workflow
progress by scanning Claude Code's workflow state files.

Usage:
    python scripts/workflow-dashboard.py [--port 10001]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from http.server import HTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

CLAUDE_PROJECTS = Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects"
PORT = int(os.environ.get("DASHBOARD_PORT", "10001"))


def find_workflow_runs() -> list[dict]:
    """Scan all Claude project dirs for workflow state files."""
    runs = []
    if not CLAUDE_PROJECTS.exists():
        return runs
    for project in CLAUDE_PROJECTS.iterdir():
        if not project.is_dir():
            continue
        for session in project.iterdir():
            wf_base = session / "workflows"
            if not wf_base.exists():
                continue
            for wf_file in sorted(wf_base.glob("wf_*.json"), reverse=True):
                try:
                    data = json.loads(wf_file.read_text())
                except Exception:
                    continue
                progress = data.get("workflowProgress", [])
                agents = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_agent"]
                active = sum(
                    1 for a in agents if a.get("state") in ("running", "queued")
                )
                done = sum(1 for a in agents if a.get("state") == "done")
                phases = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_phase"]
                current_phase = phases[-1]["title"] if phases else "—"
                runs.append(
                    {
                        "id": data.get("runId", wf_file.stem),
                        "path": str(wf_file),
                        "name": data.get("workflowName", "unknown"),
                        "status": data.get("status", "unknown"),
                        "project": project.name[:40],
                        "mtime": wf_file.stat().st_mtime,
                        "total_agents": len(agents),
                        "active": active,
                        "done": done,
                        "phase": current_phase,
                        "tokens": data.get("totalTokens", 0),
                        "duration_ms": data.get("durationMs", 0),
                        "model": data.get("defaultModel", ""),
                    }
                )
    runs.sort(key=lambda r: r["mtime"], reverse=True)
    return runs[:30]


def get_workflow_detail(wf_path: str) -> dict:
    """Read full workflow state for detail view."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(Path(wf_path).read_text())
    except Exception:
        return {"error": "cannot read workflow state"}

    progress = data.get("workflowProgress", [])
    phases_raw = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_phase"]
    agents_raw = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_agent"]

    phases = []
    for ph in phases_raw:
        ph_agents = [a for a in agents_raw if a.get("phaseIndex") == ph.get("index")]
        phases.append(
            {
                "title": ph.get("title", ""),
                "index": ph.get("index", 0),
                "agents": [
                    {
                        "label": a.get("label", ""),
                        "state": a.get("state", "unknown"),
                        "model": (a.get("model") or "")
                        .replace("claude-", "")
                        .replace("-4-6", "")
                        .replace("-4-5-20251001", ""),
                        "tokens": a.get("tokens", 0),
                        "tool_calls": a.get("toolCalls", 0),
                        "duration_s": round((a.get("durationMs") or 0) / 1000, 1),
                        "last_tool": a.get("lastToolName", ""),
                        "last_summary": (a.get("lastToolSummary") or "")[:80],
                        "prompt_preview": (a.get("promptPreview") or "")[:200],
                        "result_preview": (a.get("resultPreview") or "")[:200],
                        "attempt": a.get("attempt", 1),
                    }
                    for a in ph_agents
                ],
            }
        )

    # Orphan agents (no matching phase)
    placed = {a.get("agentId") for ph in phases for a in ph.get("agents", [])}
    orphans = [a for a in agents_raw if a.get("agentId") not in placed]

    return {
        "id": data.get("runId", ""),
        "name": data.get("workflowName", ""),
        "status": data.get("status", "unknown"),
        "total_agents": len(agents_raw),
        "total_tokens": data.get("totalTokens", 0),
        "total_tool_calls": data.get("totalToolCalls", 0),
        "duration_ms": data.get("durationMs", 0),
        "model": data.get("defaultModel", ""),
        "logs": data.get("logs", []),
        "phases": phases,
        "summary": data.get("summary", ""),
    }


def get_metrics() -> dict:
    """Aggregate metrics across all workflow runs."""
    runs = []
    if not CLAUDE_PROJECTS.exists():
        return {}
    for project in CLAUDE_PROJECTS.iterdir():
        if not project.is_dir():
            continue
        for session in project.iterdir():
            wf_base = session / "workflows"
            if not wf_base.exists():
                continue
            for wf_file in wf_base.glob("wf_*.json"):
                try:
                    runs.append(json.loads(wf_file.read_text()))
                except Exception:
                    continue

    if not runs:

"""workflow-dashboard.py — Real-time web dashboard for datum TDD workflows.

Serves a single-page dashboard on port 10001 that shows inflight workflow
progress by scanning Claude Code's workflow state files.

Usage:
    python scripts/workflow-dashboard.py [--port 10001]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from http.server import HTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlparse

CLAUDE_PROJECTS = Path.home() / ".claude" / "projects"
PORT = int(os.environ.get("DASHBOARD_PORT", "10001"))


def find_workflow_runs() -> list[dict]:
    """Scan all Claude project dirs for workflow state files."""
    runs = []
    if not CLAUDE_PROJECTS.exists():
        return runs
    for project in CLAUDE_PROJECTS.iterdir():
        if not project.is_dir():
            continue
        for session in project.iterdir():
            wf_base = session / "workflows"
            if not wf_base.exists():
                continue
            for wf_file in sorted(wf_base.glob("wf_*.json"), reverse=True):
                try:
                    data = json.loads(wf_file.read_text())
                except Exception:
                    continue
                progress = data.get("workflowProgress", [])
                agents = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_agent"]
                active = sum(
                    1 for a in agents if a.get("state") in ("running", "queued")
                )
                done = sum(1 for a in agents if a.get("state") == "done")
                phases = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_phase"]
                current_phase = phases[-1]["title"] if phases else "—"
                runs.append(
                    {
                        "id": data.get("runId", wf_file.stem),
                        "path": str(wf_file),
                        "name": data.get("workflowName", "unknown"),
                        "status": data.get("status", "unknown"),
                        "project": project.name[:40],
                        "mtime": wf_file.stat().st_mtime,
                        "total_agents": len(agents),
                        "active": active,
                        "done": done,
                        "phase": current_phase,
                        "tokens": data.get("totalTokens", 0),
                        "duration_ms": data.get("durationMs", 0),
                        "model": data.get("defaultModel", ""),
                    }
                )
    runs.sort(key=lambda r: r["mtime"], reverse=True)
    return runs[:30]


def get_workflow_detail(wf_path: str) -> dict:
    """Read full workflow state for detail view."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(Path(wf_path).read_text())
    except Exception:
        return {"error": "cannot read workflow state"}

    progress = data.get("workflowProgress", [])
    phases_raw = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_phase"]
    agents_raw = [p for p in progress if p.get("type") == "workflow_agent"]

    phases = []
    for ph in phases_raw:
        ph_agents = [a for a in agents_raw if a.get("phaseIndex") == ph.get("index")]
        phases.append(
            {
                "title": ph.get("title", ""),
                "index": ph.get("index", 0),
                "agents": [
                    {
                        "label": a.get("label", ""),
                        "state": a.get("state", "unknown"),
                        "model": (a.get("model") or "")
                        .replace("claude-", "")
                        .replace("-4-6", "")
                        .replace("-4-5-20251001", ""),
                        "tokens": a.get("tokens", 0),
                        "tool_calls": a.get("toolCalls", 0),
                        "duration_s": round((a.get("durationMs") or 0) / 1000, 1),
                        "last_tool": a.get("lastToolName", ""),
                        "last_summary": (a.get("lastToolSummary") or "")[:80],
                        "prompt_preview": (a.get("promptPreview") or "")[:200],
                        "result_preview": (a.get("resultPreview") or "")[:200],
                        "attempt": a.get("attempt", 1),
                    }
                    for a in ph_agents
                ],
            }
        )

    # Orphan agents (no matching phase)
    placed = {a.get("agentId") for ph in phases for a in ph.get("agents", [])}
    orphans = [a for a in agents_raw if a.get("agentId") not in placed]

    return {
        "id": data.get("runId", ""),
        "name": data.get("workflowName", ""),
        "status": data.get("status", "unknown"),
        "total_agents": len(agents_raw),
        "total_tokens": data.get("totalTokens", 0),
        "total_tool_calls": data.get("totalToolCalls", 0),
        "duration_ms": data.get("durationMs", 0),
        "model": data.get("defaultModel", ""),
        "logs": data.get("logs", []),
        "phases": phases,
        "summary": data.get("summary", ""),
    }


def get_metrics() -> dict:
    """Aggregate metrics across all workflow runs."""
    runs = []
    if not CLAUDE_PROJECTS.exists():
        return {}
    for project in CLAUDE_PROJECTS.iterdir():
        if not project.is_dir():
            continue
        for session in project.iterdir():
            wf_base = session / "workflows"
            if not wf_base.exists():
                continue
            for wf_file in wf_base.glob("wf_*.json"):
                try:
                    runs.append(json.loads(wf_file.read_text()))
                except Exception:
                    continue

    if not runs:
        return {"total_runs": 0}

    model_stats: dict[str, dict] = {}
    phase_stats: dict[str, dict] = {}
    agent_tokens: list[int] = []
    agent_durations: list[float] = []
    retries = 0
    total_agents = 0
    total_tokens = 0
    total_duration = 0
    status_counts: dict[str, int] = {}

    for run in runs:
        status = run.get("status", "unknown")
        status_counts[status] = status_counts.get(status, 0) + 1
        total_tokens += run.get("totalTokens", 0)
        total_duration += run.get("durationMs", 0)

        for entry in run.get("workflowProgress", []):
            if entry.get("type") != "workflow_agent":
                continue
            total_agents += 1
            model = (entry.get("model") or "unknown").replace("claude-", "")
            tokens = entry.get("tokens", 0)
            dur = entry.get("durationMs", 0)
            attempt = entry.get("attempt", 1)
            state = entry.get("state", "unknown")
            phase = entry.get("phaseTitle", "unknown")

            if tokens > 0:
                agent_tokens.append(tokens)
            if dur > 0:
                agent_durations.append(dur / 1000)

            if attempt > 1:
                retries += 1

            if model not in model_stats:
                model_stats[model] = {
                    "agents": 0,
                    "tokens": 0,
                    "duration_ms": 0,
                    "successes": 0,
                    "failures": 0,
                    "retries": 0,
                }
            model_stats[model]["agents"] += 1
            model_stats[model]["tokens"] += tokens
            model_stats[model]["duration_ms"] += dur
            if state == "done":
                model_stats[model]["successes"] += 1
            elif state in ("error", "failed"):
                model_stats[model]["failures"] += 1
            if attempt > 1:
                model_stats[model]["retries"] += 1

            if phase not in phase_stats:
                phase_stats[phase] = {
                    "agents": 0,
                    "tokens": 0,
                    "duration_ms": 0,
                    "retries": 0,
                }
            phase_stats[phase]["agents"] += 1
            phase_stats[phase]["tokens"] += tokens
            phase_stats[phase]["duration_ms"] += dur
            if attempt > 1:
                phase_stats[phase]["retries"] += 1

    models = []
    for name, s in sorted(model_stats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]["tokens"]):
        total = s["successes"] + s["failures"]
        models.append(
            {
                "model": name,
                "agents": s["agents"],
                "tokens": s["tokens"],
                "duration_ms": s["duration_ms"],
                "avg_tokens": round(s["tokens"] / s["agents"]) if s["agents"] else 0,
                "avg_duration_s": (
                    round(s["duration_ms"] / s["agents"] / 1000, 1)
                    if s["agents"]
                    else 0
                ),
                "success_rate": round(s["successes"] / total * 100) if total else 0,
                "retries": s["retries"],
            }
        )

    phases_out = []
    for name, s in sorted(phase_stats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]["tokens"]):
        phases_out.append(
            {
                "phase": name,
                "agents": s["agents"],
                "tokens": s["tokens"],
                "avg_tokens": round(s["tokens"] / s["agents"]) if s["agents"] else 0,
                "retries": s["retries"],
                "retry_rate": (
                    round(s["retries"] / s["agents"] * 100, 1) if s["agents"] else 0
                ),
            }
        )

    sorted_tokens = sorted(agent_tokens)
    median_tokens = sorted_tokens[len(sorted_tokens) // 2] if sorted_tokens else 0
    sorted_dur = sorted(agent_durations)
    median_dur = sorted_dur[len(sorted_dur) // 2] if sorted_dur else 0

    return {
        "total_runs": len(runs),
        "status_counts": status_counts,
        "total_agents": total_agents,
        "total_tokens": total_tokens,
        "total_duration_ms": total_duration,
        "total_retries": retries,
        "retry_rate": round(retries / total_agents * 100, 1) if total_agents else 0,
        "median_tokens": median_tokens,
        "median_duration_s": round(median_dur, 1),
        "models": models,
        "phases": phases_out,
        "token_distribution": sorted_tokens[:500],
        "duration_distribution": [round(d, 1) for d in sorted_dur[:500]],
    }

    """Assign a complexity tier based on parsed classification metadata.

    Returns ``{"tier": str, "signals": dict, "pipeline_shape": str}``.

    Threshold rules (using ``<`` for patch ceiling, ``>=`` for system floor):
    - **patch**: ``estimated_loc < patch_max_loc`` AND
      ``clusters_touched <= patch_max_clusters`` AND ``not new_public_api``
    - **system**: ``clusters_touched >= system_min_clusters`` OR
      (``new_public_api`` AND ``estimated_loc >= system_min_loc_with_api``)
    - **feature**: everything else

    When a field is ``None`` (missing from the spec), the change is
    conservatively routed to the **feature** tier.
    """
    thresholds = {**DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS, **(config or {})}

    loc = metadata.get("estimated_loc")
    clusters = metadata.get("clusters_touched")
    new_api = metadata.get("new_public_api")

    signals = {k: v for k, v in metadata.items() if k in _ALL_FIELDS}

    # If critical signals are missing, default to feature (safe middle ground)
    if loc is None or clusters is None:
        tier = "feature"
    else:
        is_system = clusters >= thresholds["system_min_clusters"] or (
            bool(new_api) and loc >= thresholds["system_min_loc_with_api"]
        )
        is_patch = (
            loc < thresholds["patch_max_loc"]
            and clusters <= thresholds["patch_max_clusters"]
            and not new_api
        )

        if is_system:
            tier = "system"
        elif is_patch:
